summary: Intro/discovery call between Redwood (AE+SE) and SkyBridge Cloud to explore a partnership for GPU hosting and marketplace integration. Discussed product fit (Dedicated, Private), technical integration points (VPC peering, VPN, marketplace images), typical deployment footprints, and go-to-market models (referral vs reseller). Agreed on follow-ups: share decks, perf numbers, and schedule SE deep-dive.

performance and sizing for GPU instances
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (SkyBridge Head of Partnerships), Rina Matsuda (SkyBridge Cloud Solutions Architect), Marcus Hayes (SkyBridge VP BD)

00:00 - Ethan Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; super excited to chat with SkyBridge, um, quick intros?
00:08 - Liam O'Connor: Yeah hi I'm Liam, run partnerships at SkyBridge, we've been talking about expanding our GPU marketplace offers, nice to meet you all.
00:15 - Priya Kapoor: Hi I'm Priya, I'm an SE on Redwood's infra team, I work on Dedicated and Private deployments.
00:22 - Rina Matsuda: Rina here, architect on cloud integrations, focused on image/marketplace flows and security.
00:30 - Marcus Hayes: Marcus here, quick note on commercial interest, curious on revenue share models.
00:38 - Ethan Morales: Great; agenda — quick intros, product fit, technical integration, security, and then go-to-market models and next steps. Sound OK?
00:46 - Liam O'Connor: Sounds good.
01:02 - Priya Kapoor: I'll jump in on technical bits as we go.

02:05 - Ethan Morales: To set context, Redwood is a developer-first inference platform. We offer hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private deployments — VPC/on-prem. Our customers choose depending on isolation and throughput needs.
02:22 - Rina Matsuda: When you say Dedicated, is that a managed pool we can resell as a SkyBridge offering or is it more of a Redwood-managed service?
02:30 - Ethan Morales: Good question. Dedicated is reserved capacity for a customer tier; for a partner model we have options — either we do a reseller arrangement where SkyBridge would provision and operate Redwood Dedicated stacks on your infra, or we can do referral/marketplace where traffic routes to Redwood-hosted Dedicated. We can support both, depends on compliance and go-to-market.
02:50 - Marcus Hayes: Is private deployment something we could co-package? e.g., customers buy a SkyBridge instance with Redwood Private preinstalled?
02:58 - Priya Kapoor: Yes, Private is customer-managed control plane but we can provide images and an operator bundle. There are requirements around networking — VPC peering, route tables, KMS integration for key management, etc. We typically provide an installer and Terraform modules.
03:18 - Liam O'Connor: Ok, the marketplace angle — we'd like a first-class marketplace image, and ideally some kind of automated onboarding. How heavy is the infra footprint for a reference deployment?
03:28 - Priya Kapoor: Very workload-dependent; for typical LLM inference we see reference footprints: small model dev starts with 1-2 GPUs per node, for medium production 4-8 GPUs (A100/T4 depending on model). For large scale we recommend dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling. We can share our perf sheet.
03:45 - Rina Matsuda: Can you share KV cache behavior and prefix caching? We have customers who care about latency and cost tradeoffs.
03:52 - Priya Kapoor: Yes, we do KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated token compute; it helps on chatty workloads. Also batching config and quantization profiles matter — e.g., int8 quant can reduce memory and cost but you need to validate quality.

05:10 - Ethan Morales: On integration specifics: for marketplace images we provide AMI/container images, and a small operator that handles model artifacts and routing. For SkyBridge we can embed an image and a quickstart in the marketplace listing, plus a guided flow for registering tenants.
05:28 - Liam O'Connor: Good. From a security perspective — SOC2 and ISO? We've got enterprise customers asking for auditability.
05:33 - Ethan Morales: We are SOC 2 Type II compliant, we also have audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and SSO via SAML/Okta. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and we can hand over audit logs for the tenant.
05:50 - Rina Matsuda: On SSO, how does RBAC map for multi-tenant setups?
05:55 - Priya Kapoor: We support RBAC at route/model level; for private installs, RBAC usually integrates with your IdP and we map groups to roles. Some of the mappings are custom so we usually prototype during the POC.

07:10 - Marcus Hayes: Commercially, what's the typical revenue split for a reseller? Do you have standard partner T&Cs?
07:18 - Ethan Morales: We have flexible partner programs: referral (finder's fee) or reseller (discounted price to partner with a contractual rev share). We can share partner tier docs; specifics vary by region and commitment.
07:29 - Liam O'Connor: We have some customers in EMEA who require data residency — any constraints?
07:35 - Priya Kapoor: We can deploy in regional clouds and support VPC peering inside region; for hosted Redwood we'd need to confirm region availability. For Private, that constraint is solved since it's deployed in-customer or in SkyBridge region.

09:00 - Rina Matsuda: For the operator, is there an automated model onboarding pipeline? Our marketplace buyer would expect easy model uploads and version pinning.
09:10 - Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have model catalog tools and version pinning; also rollout policies for canary or A/B tests, and automatic fallback. We also expose APIs to push artifacts.
09:22 - Liam O'Connor: Any concerns around licensing for model bundles in marketplace?
09:26 - Ethan Morales: Licensing is up to the model owner; many open models are fine but for commercial models you need the license. We can help with packaging.

11:00 - Rina Matsuda: On perf: can you provide rough throughput/latency for e.g., a 70B model on 8xA100?
11:09 - Priya Kapoor: Rough ballpark — low latency chat workloads we aim <150ms per token for certain configs with optimizations; throughput depends on batch size; we'll send detailed perf numbers. Caveat: numbers vary with sequence length and tokenizer behavior.
11:25 - Marcus Hayes: Do you do benchmarks against other infra providers?
11:28 - Ethan Morales: We have internal benchmarks vs some clouds and other inference runtimes; we can share sanitized results. We also have a partner list — some of your competitors we know (ApexCloud, Aurora GPU, NimbusCompute).

13:05 - Liam O'Connor: For onboarding a SkyBridge marketplace seller, what would a POC look like? Timeline?
13:12 - Priya Kapoor: Typical POC: 1) define success criteria (throughput/latency/cost), 2) spin up a reference environment (2-8 GPUs), 3) run a small benchmark with your sample workload, 4) validate security controls. Usually 2-4 weeks.
13:28 - Rina Matsuda: We need to know networking requirements for peering and private link.
13:33 - Priya Kapoor: We'll supply network diagrams: ports, subnets, peering requirements, plus optional VPN. For Private installs there's a small set of NAT/firewall rules and an installer that uses Terraform/Ansible.

15:00 - Ethan Morales: Quick question — are you more interested in a reseller model where SkyBridge installs Redwood Private for customers, or in a marketplace listing that points to Redwood-hosted services?
15:12 - Liam O'Connor: We want both options, but initially marketplace referral makes sense for speed. Reseller is longer-term for enterprise customers that demand on-prem.
15:21 - Marcus Hayes: Agreed, start with marketplace and then pilot reseller for a few key accounts.

17:10 - Rina Matsuda: Compliance — do you have SOC/ISO docs we can attach to our partner compliance checklist?
17:15 - Ethan Morales: Yes, we'll share SOC2 attestation and a security pack. For Private we'll provide deployment guidance and cust KMS integration notes.

19:00 - Priya Kapoor: On the tech deep-dive, we'd like access to your infra team to talk about automation and images, possibly credentials to test a staging image.
19:10 - Rina Matsuda: We can arrange staging access; I'll follow up with the infra team's contact.

21:03 - Ethan Morales: Other technical note: model quantization and kernel selection can be tuned per hardware; if you want to support multiple GPU types (A100, H100, etc.), there are different kernels and we can help validate.
21:20 - Priya Kapoor: Also routing policies — we can route by latency vs cost and have fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained; that's useful for marketplace users to meet SLAs.

23:30 - Liam O'Connor: From GTM standpoint, what marketing assets do partners typically need?
23:36 - Ethan Morales: Partner one-pager, co-branded case study template, joint webinars, and a marketplace listing guide. We'll provide a partner kit.

25:00 - Marcus Hayes: On pricing — do you list MSRP or is it negotiation per deal?
25:05 - Ethan Morales: Catalog pricing for self-serve, and partner discounted tiers for reseller. We can share price bands.

27:10 - Rina Matsuda: Any known pitfalls when deploying to a cloud marketplace? For instance, auto-scaling across availability zones?
27:18 - Priya Kapoor: Auto-scaling needs topology planning — GPUS don't migrate; you need capacity managers and spot/burst policies. We usually plan reserved pools and autoscaler rules to avoid cold start latency.

29:30 - Ethan Morales: Let's talk timeline: can we aim to have the partner packet and perf numbers out by Friday (2026-10-15)?
29:38 - Liam O'Connor: Yes that works for us. We'll also get back on model licensing expectations.

31:00 - Priya Kapoor: I'll attach a sample Terraform module and a reference topology for 4xA100 that folks can use.
31:08 - Rina Matsuda: Perfect.

33:20 - Marcus Hayes: Any legal stuff we need to pre-clear? NDAs? Marketplace terms?
33:26 - Ethan Morales: We can start with a mutual NDA if needed; partner agreements vary. For marketplace listing there's a standard T&Cs doc. We'll send legal contacts.

35:10 - Liam O'Connor: For the deep-dive, who should attend from Redwood? SE + product?
35:16 - Ethan Morales: SE (Priya) and product/partner manager (me) are good; for reseller we sometimes include Solutions Engineering and Legal.

37:50 - Rina Matsuda: A couple quick tech clarifications — do you have secrets management for model weights?
37:55 - Priya Kapoor: Yes, model artifacts live in secured object stores and we support encrypted volumes; for Private you can plug in your KMS.

39:40 - Marcus Hayes: Are there references of existing cloud partners we can review?
39:45 - Ethan Morales: Yes, we'll share a partner reference list; names like Aurora GPU and some smaller cloud partners — we'll sanitize customer names if needed.

41:00 - Liam O'Connor: Any other barriers you foresee on our side to run a quick POC?
41:06 - Priya Kapoor: Nothing big; just access to a staging cluster, a sample workload, and network peering. We'll coordinate.

44:00 - Ethan Morales: Ok, recap of next steps: we'll send partner one-pager, perf numbers, Terraform module, and SOC2/security pack. Priya to share perf sheet. SkyBridge to confirm reseller interest window. Schedule a technical deep-dive the week of Oct 19.
44:28 - Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
44:33 - Rina Matsuda: Thanks, talk soon.
44:36 - Marcus Hayes: Thanks all.
44:42 - Ethan Morales: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with links. Bye.

Meeting end: 16:48 UTC
notes: Shared artifacts: partner_one_pager.pdf (to be sent), perf_sheet_8xA100.xlsx (SE to share), terraform-module.zip (SE sample).
